4. That in title suit no 64 of 1995 the present respondent no 1 Mostafa Ahmed as the plaintiff stated everything in support of his claim which he stated by filing written statement in Title suit no 67 of 1995. He also stated that the present appellant Mostafa Shahriar in collusion with his alleged nephew defendant No. 1 Shahed Ahmed Chowdhury created a forged deed dated 10.11.1991 alleged to have been executed and registered by plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed in favour of defendant No. 1 Shahed Ahmed and his son has been shown as an attesting witness though he never executed and registered any deed in favour of Shahed Ahmed Chowdhury that he and his son were not present at Sylhet on that date; that the defendant in order to grab the land of the plaintiff created the aforesaid false deed; that on 10.07.1994 when the plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed was in Dhaka, the defendants Shahriar and Shahed with the help of their party men forcibly entered into the house of the plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed and dispossessed him from the house and also from the land; that on return to Sylhet when he asked the defendants about the reason they disclosed that on the basis of purchase they took possession of the same: that after enquiry on 08.08.1994 and after obtaining the certified copy he came to know that defendant No. 1 in collusion with defendant No. 2 created a forged deed dated 10.11.1991 in respect of 60 decimals of land of plot no 171; that on the basis of so-called deed dated 10.11.1991 the defendants have not acquired any title or possession and for declaration of the aforesaid deed as forged and recovery of khas possession after evicting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from the suit land of the suit he instituted T.S. No 64 of 1995. 

 13. Firstly, it appears that Liakot Ali as plaintiff No. 1 along with purchasers instituted the suit and deposed twice as P.W-2 to prove his case. His identity was not challenged by the defendants at that time. Secondly, Respondent Mostafa as defendant stated that, his vendor Liakot Ali left for Chittagong Hill Tracts and he has already died and Liakot Ali present in the Court is not the real person, trial court dis-believed his claim with cogent reasons. but, the Court of Appeal below without reversing the said findings with its own finding referring the materials on record mechanically and whimsically allowed the appeal and thereby committed serious error as revisional Court in allowing the appeals and the High Court Division com-mitted an error in failing to thresh out the said mistake of affirming the judgment of the Court of appeal below. Thirdly, it appears that the Vested Property Authority issued notice on 31.08.1978 in VP Case No. 22 of 1978-79 claiming the entire land as vested property, but, after production of the necessary papers by the appellants that notice withdrawn. However, the Court of Appeal did not consider these aspects of the case rather, the High Court Division also committed error in failing to find out the said error of the Court of appeal below and thereby committed error in affirming the decision of the Court of appeals Lastly, it appears that the plaintiff appellant filed his suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession, but the Court of appeal below decreed the suit in favour of respondent without arriving at any finding regarding his possession followed by dispossession of the suit land and the High Court Division erred in affirming such an erroneous judgment and decree.
